samples.summary: Paste calls `clearCellsUnderMerge` without a `keep` predicate, so it can delete destination cells the same paste just wrote
samples.evidence: `moveRangeTo` passes `(sref) => movedGrid.has(sref)` (sheet.ts:2542) so the move never erases the cells it just wrote; the paste call at sheet.ts:2339-2343 passes no `keep`. Any grid entry that lands on a covered cell of a propagated block is written by `setGrid` (line 2295) and then unconditionally `store.delete`d by `clearCellsUnderMerge` (only style-only cells survive). This is reachable whenever the copy buffer's snapshot is out of sync with the live merge layout: copy A1:B1 unmerged (buffer holds A1 and B1 values), then merge A1:B1, then paste at A3 — `copiedMerges` is read live so A3:B3 becomes a block and the B3 value that was just pasted is silently dropped. Same class of divergence for a covered cell that had content when copied.

samples.summary: Merge layout is read live from a stale snapshot range, so paste can create/refuse blocks that do not correspond to what was copied
samples.evidence: `const copiedMerges = this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` uses `this.copyBuffer.sourceRange`, a coordinate window captured at copy time, but reads merges as they are NOW. The comment (2201-2203) justifies this for `unmergeSelection`, but the same asymmetry cuts the other way: (a) a merge created in that coordinate window after the copy is re-created at the destination even though the buffer's cell values are pre-merge (see the data-loss path above); (b) a structural edit (`insertRows`/`moveColumns`/`shiftCells`) can slide an unrelated merge so that it only partially overlaps the stale `sourceRange`, and then the check at 2216 refuses *every* paste of that buffer forever, silently. The grid content and the merge layout should be read from the same point in time.

samples.summary: A propagated merge can be created across a frozen-pane boundary, which `canMergeSelection` explicitly forbids
samples.evidence: `canMergeSelection` (sheet.ts:4414-4422) rejects a merge that crosses `frozenRows`/`frozenCols`. The new propagation at sheet.ts:2336-2338 calls `store.setMerge`/`this.merges.set` for the translated anchor with no such check, so pasting a copied block so that it straddles the freeze line produces a merged block the merge API would never allow (the renderer draws frozen and scrolling panes separately). `moveRangeTo` has the same gap, but this change adds a second path to it.

samples.summary: Style patches are applied to existing cells before the merge layout is updated, so they normalize through the old anchors
samples.evidence: `applyStylePatchToExistingCells` (line 2305) resolves each cell through `normalizeRefToAnchor` (sheet.ts:2047), but the merge drop/create block does not run until line 2320-2346. For a paste that drops a destination block, conflicting style overrides are funneled into the soon-to-be-deleted anchor instead of the individual cells; for a paste that creates a block, they are applied to cells that are about to be cleared. The merge propagation comment at 2315-2319 explicitly orders itself before recalculation but not before the style pass.

samples.summary: A merge-refused paste is a completely silent no-op — no error, no toast, no console output
samples.evidence: `paste()` returns `false` from sheet.ts:2217 and 2287 and the views (spreadsheet.ts:717, worksheet.ts:4901) only skip `clearCopyBuffer()`. Ctrl+V then does nothing at all with no explanation; the marching ants staying up is the only signal, and for a plain (non-cut) copy that is indistinguishable from the normal post-copy state. `moveRangeTo` at least aborts a drag the user can see.

samples.summary: Returning `false` for "nothing to paste" now also suppresses `clearCopyBuffer`, changing unrelated behavior
samples.evidence: The early returns at 2173 (pivot), 2247 (no text/html) and 2254 (empty grid) all return `false`, and both views now clear the copy buffer only on `true`. Previously `paste()` always fell through to `clearCopyBuffer()`. So an attempted paste with an empty/unsupported clipboard (or on a pivot sheet) now leaves the internal buffer and marching ants alive, including for a cut, where the source now stays marked indefinitely. The refusal signal conflates 'refused by a merge' with 'nothing on the clipboard'.

finding.summary: Paste calls `clearCellsUnderMerge` without a `keep` predicate, so it can delete destination cells the same paste just wrote
finding.evidence: `moveRangeTo` passes `(sref) => movedGrid.has(sref)` (sheet.ts:2542) so the move never erases the cells it just wrote; the paste call at sheet.ts:2339-2343 passes no `keep`. Any grid entry that lands on a covered cell of a propagated block is written by `setGrid` (line 2295) and then unconditionally `store.delete`d by `clearCellsUnderMerge` (only style-only cells survive). This is reachable whenever the copy buffer's snapshot is out of sync with the live merge layout: copy A1:B1 unmerged (buffer holds A1 and B1 values), then merge A1:B1, then paste at A3 — `copiedMerges` is read live so A3:B3 becomes a block and the B3 value that was just pasted is silently dropped. Same class of divergence for a covered cell that had content when copied.

verdict.reason: The code is literally as quoted (paste calls clearCellsUnderMerge with no `keep` at sheet.ts:2336-2344 after setGrid at sheet.ts:2295, while moveRangeTo passes `keep = movedGrid.has` at sheet.ts:2538-2543), but the claimed data loss cannot occur. A grid entry can only land on a covered (non-anchor) sref of a propagated block if the copy-time snapshot held content at a source cell that is now covered by a live merge fully inside the copied range (validated at sheet.ts:2204-2224). Every merge-creating path clears that content in the live sheet first: mergeSelection deletes/reduces every non-anchor cell before setMerge (sheet.ts:4456-4471), and the paste/move propagation paths do the same via clearCellsUnderMerge (sheet.ts:2336-2344, 2528-2543); those are the only setMerge call sites in the package (sheet.ts:2337, 2533, 4470). So in the reviewer's scenario (copy A1:B1, merge A1:B1, paste at A3) the "2" was already deleted from the sheet by mergeSelection; the pasted B3 value is a stale clipboard ghost, and keeping it would put content under a merged block that resurfaces on unmerge — the exact invariant documented at sheet.ts:911-917 and asserted by merge.test.ts:265-281. The asymmetry with moveRangeTo is deliberate: there movedGrid is the only surviving copy of live cells (source deleted at sheet.ts:2498-2508), whereas paste leaves the source in place (and for a cut the source cell was already emptied when the merge was created). Nothing live is lost, nothing crashes, and no invariant is broken.

finding.summary: Merge layout is read live from a stale snapshot range, so paste can create/refuse blocks that do not correspond to what was copied
finding.evidence: `const copiedMerges = this.getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange)` uses `this.copyBuffer.sourceRange`, a coordinate window captured at copy time, but reads merges as they are NOW. The comment (2201-2203) justifies this for `unmergeSelection`, but the same asymmetry cuts the other way: (a) a merge created in that coordinate window after the copy is re-created at the destination even though the buffer's cell values are pre-merge (see the data-loss path above); (b) a structural edit (`insertRows`/`moveColumns`/`shiftCells`) can slide an unrelated merge so that it only partially overlaps the stale `sourceRange`, and then the check at 2216 refuses *every* paste of that buffer forever, silently. The grid content and the merge layout should be read from the same point in time.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described: paste's internal branch reads grid/rangeStyles from the copy-time snapshot (sheet.ts:2195-2211, populated at 2138/2151) but reads merges live through getMergesIntersecting(sourceRange) (2204, impl 888-909) against the stale copy-time coordinate window. The staleness is achievable: shiftCells rewrites the merge map (1311) for insertRows/deleteRows/insertColumns/deleteColumns (1231-1258) and moveRows/moveColumns (1263-1272), while copyBuffer.sourceRange is never re-based (only writes are 2138, 2151, 2125, 2291). A merge slid into partial overlap with the stale window then trips the check at 2216 and returns false with no fallback to the TSV path, making Ctrl+V a permanent silent no-op for that buffer; the buffer is only cleared on successful paste (view/worksheet.ts:4902, view/spreadsheet.ts:718) or Escape (view/worksheet.ts:5073-5074), so no guard prevents it. The data-drop half is also real: pastedMerges built from the live layout are applied at 2336-2344 and clearCellsUnderMerge (918-932) deletes covered cells that setGrid (2295) just wrote from the pre-merge snapshot. Reachable from real UI paste handlers; a silent break of the paste flow plus dropped copied values is blocking under the correctness rubric.

finding.summary: `rangeOf` uses argument spread (`Math.min(...rows)`) — replacing the removed loop-based `gridRange` reintroduces a stack-overflow crash on large pastes
finding.evidence: The delta deletes `gridRange` (which computed min/max with an explicit `for` loop over `grid.keys()`, safe for any size) and routes both `paste` (sheet.ts:2255) and `selectPastedRange` (sheet.ts:2389) through `rangeOf`, which does `Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)` on arrays with one element per pasted cell. V8 throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` once the spread exceeds roughly 100k arguments. A plain TSV paste of a large external CSV (e.g. 20k rows x 10 cols = 200k cells) reaches `rangeOf` with a 200k-element array and throws. The throw happens before `store.beginBatch()`, so it propagates out of `Sheet.paste` into the view's catch and the paste silently fails; in `selectPastedRange` it would throw after the write, leaving the batch already ended but the exception escaping to the view handler. The previous loop had no such limit, so this is a regression introduced by this delta.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `rangeOf` uses argument spread (`Math.min(...rows)` / `Math.max(...cols)`) over a per-cell array, reintroducing a stack-overflow `RangeError` on large pastes. The actual implementation does not do this. `packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:24-46` accumulates bounds with an explicit `for (const sref of grid.keys())` loop over `±Infinity`-initialized accumulators — no spread at all. The only occurrence of the literal text `Math.min(...` in the file is at coordinates.ts:18-20, inside the doc comment that explains the loop was chosen *specifically because* spreading a large paste's keys overflows the call stack. A repo-wide grep for `Math\.(min|max)\(\.\.\.` returns no hit in coordinates.ts code or in sheet.ts, and `rangeOf` is defined exactly once in the repository (coordinates.ts:24). There is also a passing regression test at packages/sheets/test/sheet/coordinates.test.ts:73-89 that builds a 120k-cell grid (asserting `grid.size > 100_000`) and checks `rangeOf` returns the correct bounds — the precise scenario the finding predicts would throw. The finding's secondary premises are also unfounded: the empty-grid precondition is guarded at both cited call sites, sheet.ts:2254 (`if (!pasteRange && grid.size === 0) return false;` immediately preceding the `rangeOf` call on 2255) and sheet.ts:2388 (`if (grid.size === 0) return;` immediately preceding the call on 2389). Ground: not-present.
